offline_allocation_objective: minimize sum_b w_b * epsilon_b(bits_b), subject to sum_b bits_b <= total_bit_budget and independently validated per-block residual caps
invariants: Each epsilon_b is a per-block worst-case residual certificate validated against the original payload and codebook.
Query energy weights affect bit allocation only; they do not enter the correctness proof.
For any finite query admitted by the score profile, the exact bound uses its actual ||q_b|| and stored epsilon_b values.
Distribution shift can make the chosen allocation inefficient but cannot invalidate a correct worst-case epsilon_b certificate.
Rebuilds or codebook changes create a new generation and require fresh certificate verification.
Never replace a deterministic residual certificate with a mean or percentile reconstruction error.
nonclaims: The epsilon curve is invented for this synthetic allocation example.
No actual quantizer or bit-allocation optimizer is implemented.
No benchmark speedup or residual-bound tightness result is represented.
